**Screening the four solutions**

**Solution 1 (3n+1): rejected.** Its own host graph fails. Take the clique partition {v, a₁, b₁}, {c₁}, and for each i ≥ 2 the partition {a_i, b_i}, {c_i}. The blue neighbourhood of v is c₁ together with groups 2 to n. The only blue edges inside it are the n−1 edges a_i c_i for i ≥ 2, since c₁ has no blue edge to any vertex of N_B(v). So no blue F_n is centred at v. The other vertices have blue degree at most 3, which is below 2n ≥ 4, so no blue F_n exists anywhere. The "compensating pair" step that the solution asserts is exactly where this fails, and the lower bound is only sketched.

**Solution 2 (3n+4): accepted as the most likely correct answer.** The construction K₁ + (n+1)P₃ on 3n+4 vertices works. Any clique of F avoiding the centre c lies inside a single P₃. A clique containing c is {c}, {c, x}, or {c, x, y} with xy an edge of one P₃. So at least n whole P₃'s are untouched by c's cluster, each gives a blue edge under any partition, and c is blue-adjacent to all of them. That yields a blue induced F_n. The lower bound is hand-waved, so the solution is not fully proven. Its value is also consistent with the problem's restriction to n ≥ 2. I could not fully verify that 3n+3 vertices are insufficient.

**Solution 3 (3): rejected.** It solves a different problem (speed-doubling assistants on a cube) and is off-target.

**Solution 4 (2n+2): rejected.** Its upper bound fails. Take the proposed graph on 2n+2 vertices and colour c₁v₁, c₁w₁, c₂v₂, c₂w₂ red, everything else blue. Each red neighbourhood is a clique ({v₁,w₁} at c₁, {v₂,w₂} at c₂, single vertices elsewhere), so there is no red induced K₁,₂. The centre c₁ has only n−1 full blue pairs, and every other vertex has blue degree at most 3 < 2n. So there is no blue induced F_n, and 2n+2 vertices do not suffice.

**Conclusion:** Solution 2 is the only one whose final answer survives checking. Its construction is valid, and I believe 3n+4 is the correct value, though I have not verified the matching lower bound.

CHOICE: 2
